items.title: Luis Conte interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 24, 2025
items.q: we would see Celia Cruz and you know the greats before they left Cuba, before they passed.

ctx.x: That’s so interesting. I was wondering, because I was thinking of a question about that because from my standpoint the music that you were listening to, which I also loved, would be considered simpler than Cuban dance music and did that occur to you later on? That the music of your own country was more complex, or am I off base here?

Yeah, I mean once I got out here and I started you know getting into music and now we start dealing with Latin music, Cuban music, the first thing I hear is guys going – well is this three-two or two-three? For example. And I’m going what are you talking about? I © Fillius Jazz Archive -3-

mean play what you were playing [claps]. I said no, no, no but so you realize, that’s when I realized man, a lot of people – I mean and I would hear other musicians go like yeah, Latin music, nobody plays one. That’s another common thing I would hear. But to me it was just like what it was. Because in Cuba I earlier said I didn’t pay much attention to it, I was paying attention to it by osmosis because it was around, you know. And my parents, the other thing about my parents is they loved to hear bands and see…
